questions.question: What does a fact table primarily record?
What is the main role of a dimension?
options: Provide descriptive context for filtering and grouping facts
Append one row for every query

questions.question: Why should conversions and visits be stored instead of only conversion rate?
options: The additive components permit correctly weighted aggregation

questions.question: One segment has 1 conversion from 10 visits and another has 50 from 100. What is the combined conversion rate?
Why do warehouse dimensions often use surrogate keys?
options: To support source integration and historical versions independently of business keys
To prevent dimensions from containing attributes

questions.question: What is a table's grain?
options: The exact statement of what one row represents

questions.question: An order has three lines and shipping cost 12 is repeated on each line. What naïve sum results?
Why is atomic grain often valuable?
options: It preserves detail that can be rolled up into many analyses

questions.question: Ten order lines join directly to three promotions for the same order. How many rows can the join produce?
What is the strongest automated enforcement of a declared order-line grain?
options: A comment saying duplicates are unlikely
A uniqueness test on the columns that identify one line

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: What characterizes a star schema?
options: A central fact joins directly to relatively denormalized dimensions
Every dimension attribute has its own fact table
All facts are stored as JSON arrays

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: What characterizes a snowflake dimension?
options: Its descriptive hierarchies are normalized into additional joined tables
It requires one row per query

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: Why can repeated labels in a star dimension cost less storage than expected?
options: Columnar compression handles repeated values efficiently

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: When is selective snowflaking most justified?
options: Whenever third normal form is possible
When all dimensions have one row
When a hierarchy has independent governance, reuse, or structural complexity

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: Why can normalizing category into a separate table still produce historically wrong reports?
options: An in-place category hierarchy change can reclassify old facts without temporal versioning
Facts cannot join to normalized dimensions

questions.topic: Star Schema vs Snowflake: The Join-Cost Tradeoff
questions.question: Which evidence should drive the final star-versus-snowflake decision?
options: The diagram with the fewest boxes only
Query patterns, governance needs, measured plans, and fanout safety
A rule that every warehouse must be fully normalized
